eye: eyes, adults of both sexes (holotype female plus paratypes)
method: taxonomic description of preserved specimens from deep-sea samples
conditions: New species described from the female holotype (3 mm, ZMH K-47225; IceAGE station 1057, 2504 m, south-west of Iceland) and paratypes: 2 males (3 mm) and 2 females (3 and 4 mm) on slides from BioIce station 2367 (719 m), Mareano station R1225-RP112 (401 m) and IceAGE station 1006 (1386 m), plus 8 wet-sample specimens from Svalbard waters (819 m). The Description (Head) states 'Eyes absent.' for the pooled material; the Abstract separates the species from A. manudens by 'the absence of eyes' and the name refers to it. Table 2 contrasts A. manudens (eyes round, strongly coloured) and A. hamatus (eyes ill defined, bean-shaped or oval). Not a cave species: Atlantic deep-water samples. The paper does not state the number of specimens checked for eyes.

conditions: Redescription (Description, Head) of Amphilochus hamatus (Stephensen, 1925), comb. n. (formerly Amphilochopsis hamatus), drawings made from four specimens IINH37894, IINH37898, IINH37900 and IINH37903 (BioIce stations 2077, 2236, 2318, 2367, Iceland waters); type material not examined; sexes of the drawn specimens not given in the text read. Table 2 lists the eyes as 'ill defined, bean-shaped or oval', while the sibling A. anoculus has none and A. manudens has round, strongly coloured eyes. The paper does not say whether eye visibility varies between specimens.

value: eyes reduced to an eyeplate; the cornea-like lateral portions are brilliant red in living specimens and feign functional eyes
eye: eyeplate with cornea-like lateral portions, adult and subadult females (holotype description)
method: taxonomic description of the holotype, with live colour from dive photographs
conditions: Description of the spent female holotype (body length 26.8 mm, NHMW 27296, dive 612, 15 Jan 2016, 10 m) from an ice cave NE of Claude Bernard Island, Adelie Land, East Antarctica; one subadult female paratype (21.5 mm, NHMW 27297) from the same cave. Only these two females are known; males are unknown. The next sentence in the same paragraph says the eyeplates become transparent after slide embedding and bleaching, with 'neither functional nor both vestigial ommatidia and neuronal structures visible'; the Diagnosis calls the cornea-like lateral portions separated by sulci from the main part of the eyeplate, and the genus Diagnosis gives eyes of Pseudomma as reduced to a single eyeplate without visual elements (genus level, not used for the value).

value: eye rudiments without visual elements, subovate, converging at the mesial third and hispid all around with scales
eye: eye rudiments, adult and subadult females
method: taxonomic description of preserved deep-sea specimens
conditions: Diagnosis based on adult and subadult females (the paper says so). Holotype adult female (body length 25.8 mm, ZMH 64653, ANDEEP-I station 046-7, Drake Passage, 2894 m) with 6 further paratype lots of females, immatures and juveniles from the Drake Passage, Weddell Abyssal Plain and South Sandwich Trench (3683 to 4698 m); males unknown. The holotype Description adds that the eye rudiments are dorsoventrally compressed by a factor of 1.7 to 1.8 and carry a single triangular ocular papilla covered by spiniform scales. The paper does not state how many of the specimens were checked for visual elements.

value: ommatidia without rhabdom that still form a compact, laterally positioned cornea delimited from the eyestalk
method: supplementary description of preserved deep-sea specimens, with microscopy of the eye
conditions: First description of non-adult males: one immature male (body length 13.4 mm, on slides; ANDEEP-II station 135-4, northern Weddell Abyssal Plain, 4678 m) and the posterior part of one subadult male from ANDEEP-III station 088-8 (4930 m); one immature female (10.3 mm) is also noted. Adults are not described here. The neighbouring sentence says the cornea is opaque and the eyestalk shows a pattern of transparent and opaque parts. The paper's wording does not say whether adults keep the rhabdom-free ommatidia.

value: eye round and protruding, near the front of the head
eye: eye, adult males and females of the type series (9 fish)
conditions: Description covers the holotype (male, standard length 83.3 mm, ZIN 56687) and 8 paratypes (SL 48.7 to 81.0 mm, ZIN 56688), all from the Krasnaya River near Tokarevka, Kaliningrad Region, Russia, 31 Aug. 2019; sexes of the paratypes are not given in the text read. Horizontal eye diameter 6.9 to 7.9 % SL (mean 7.3 +/- 0.3, n = 9) in the tables; the sentence gives the mean 7.3 % SL and, for the holotype, 7.4 % SL or 22.4 % head length. The Diagnosis and Abstract call the eyes 'round, protruding (tubular)' and the etymology refers to round, convex eyes; the Discussion contrasts Cottus microstomus (eye oval, not bulging). Interorbital space on average 1.5 times narrower than the eye diameter. The sample is one river population; no live eye observations.
